novelty_flags.label: related_work; literature_map; thm:identification-frontier gap
novelty_flags.one_line: Wood1999BinomialMixtures conflates Wood’s 1999 Annals of Statistics article with the distinct 1992 Annals of Probability article: the cited DOI/version is the former, whose title, pages, and Theorems 1–2 are not “Binomial mixtures and finite exchangeability.”

soundness_flags.label: lem:scm-moment-reduction and def:hierarchical-scm-class
soundness_flags.one_line: The five class properties do not state that Q_i is the conditional four-cell law of O_ij, so they permit Q_i labels unrelated to Pr(O_ij=(a,y)|Q_i) and do not imply the asserted Bernstein moment reduction.

soundness_flags.label: ass:strict-overlap
soundness_flags.one_line: μ(K_epsilon)=1 is automatic from the declared type μ ∈ P(K_epsilon); either define μ on the ambient simplex and impose overlap, or remove this redundant assumption.

soundness_flags.label: thm:whole-set-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: With C_n,alpha defined as the union of every fiber over R_n,alpha ∩ B_m,epsilon, coverage follows immediately from b ∈ R_n,alpha and b ∈ B_m,epsilon, so this is a definitional corollary rather than an independent theorem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1706–1710, title and Introduction; journal text identifies Theorems 1–2 as Section 5 convergence results
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The DOI resolves to “Binomial mixtures: geometric estimation of the mixing distribution,” Annals of Statistics 27(5):1706–1721; it states that an exact binomial mixture determines only the first n moments, while the distinct “Binomial mixtures and finite exchangeability” article is Wood 1992, Annals of Probability 20(3):1167–1173.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 256, article 106254, 2026; theorem-text comparison corroborated against arXiv:2111.05243v2
source_verification_receipts.locator: arXiv v2 pp. 15 and 18–19, Proposition 1 and Proposition 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives valid ATE bounds built from order-q pooling polynomials and compares their local width properties; it does not state sharp optimization over a full latent mixing-law fiber.
Relative-interior moment data yield dual attainment, and Corollary 5.9 supplies a feasible representing measure detecting every nonzero nonnegative continuous function.

source_verification_receipts.version: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 134(10), 2006
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves a finite atomic cubature rule preserving a finite polynomial function system.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(547), 2024; published online 2023
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper reduces discrete causal inference problems to polynomial optimization and reports valid non-sharp and epsilon-sharp numerical bounds; it does not provide exact CAD recovery for continuous atom locations.
Bugni develops bootstrap inference aimed at coverage of an identified set in models defined by finitely many moment inequalities.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 35(2), 2026
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article constructs pointwise CDF and quantile confidence intervals for an unrestricted univariate binomial mixing distribution by exact composite-test inversion.
The paper develops convex-optimization duality for optimal probability inequalities under prescribed moments, rather than hierarchical causal-fiber semantics.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add primitive calibration conditions, separately stating Q_i ∼ μ and Pr(O_ij=(a,y) | Q_i=q)=q_ay; then make the hierarchical class depend on them and recheck the converse SCM construction.
Replace the Wood entry with the actual 1999 geometric-estimation citation and separately cite Wood 1992 for finite exchangeability, with theorem/page anchors matched to the claims used.

Demote whole-set coverage to a corollary and make the inference contribution substantive: for example, prove an implementable finite-complexity inversion/CAD procedure or a strict comparison with a named endpoint-wise interval method.

recommended_next_step: Revise the SCM calibration and redundant-overlap specification, correct the Wood literature record, and recast the definitional coverage claim before advancing to Stage 0.
